solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post, which drops the counts, so each count is read off the blogger's answer

clue.text: Middle week is covered by administrative trainee

indicators.note: the word before 'covered by' sits under a lid, so it goes inside the letters that follow

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for week
taken as written
AT is the abbreviation for an administrative trainee

explanation.surface: A junior office trainee has been given the job of handling the midweek paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' of 'is covered by' is not a link word but the letters that get covered. With 5-across this top row puns on 'waste ground'.
explanation.definitionFit: The waist is the narrow central part of the body, so it is the body's middle.

clue.text: Refinement of Walter Scott's prime ne'er-do-well

indicators.note: a refinement reworks material into a new form, so the letters that follow are rearranged
the prime part of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of Scott

explanation.surface: A literary judgement that the novelist Walter Scott polished up his best good-for-nothing character.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastrel is a worthless idler, a good-for-nothing who wastes his life.

clue.text: In London suburb I bale out giving legal ground

indicators.note: something in a place is inside it, so the letter goes within the suburb
out here means disordered, so the letters before it are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: Acton is a district of west London
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suburban Londoner bails out of a deal, giving someone grounds to sue.
explanation.walkthrough: Acton is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something actionable affords grounds for a lawsuit, so it provides a legal basis to sue.

clue.text: Train of silk except that it could've been blown

blocks.note: a sack was a loose silk gown with a train falling from the shoulders
but can mean except that

explanation.surface: A wedding train made of silk, except that the wind might have whipped it away.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition's past tense says the instrument belongs to an earlier age.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut was the Renaissance forerunner of the trombone, an instrument played by blowing.

clue.text: Ignoring one very frivolous comedy actor who may sing

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so these letters are dropped from the word that follows

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
V is an abbreviation for very
trivial means frivolous, lacking seriousness

explanation.surface: A light-hearted comic actor who sings, unless one leaves out the silliness.
explanation.walkthrough: A trial is a light comic tenor role in French opera, named after the singer Antoine Trial.
explanation.definitionFit: In opera a trial is a comic tenor part, so it names a singing comedy performer.

clue.text: Credit admitted is knocked on the head

blocks.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
to own up to something is to admit it

explanation.surface: A confession is acknowledged and the whole matter is promptly killed off.
explanation.walkthrough: With 1-across the top row sounds like 'waste ground'.
explanation.definitionFit: To crown someone is informal slang for hitting them over the head, so a person struck on the skull has been crowned.

clue.text: Hybrid canine found by explorer

blocks.note: C is the dental notation for a canine tooth
James Clark Ross and his uncle John Ross were polar explorers

explanation.surface: A mixed-breed dog discovered by an adventurer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' looks like a dog, which fits the hybrid, but it is a tooth abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross is an animal or plant bred from two different varieties, which is a hybrid.

clue.text: King Lear roughly captures capital — Rob Roy's rougher

indicators.note: something done roughly is not in its proper form, so the letters of the name are muddled
one thing that captures another holds it inside

blocks.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king
taken as written
UC stands for upper case, capital letters

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's King Lear storms a capital in a rough fashion, making him wilder than Rob Roy.
explanation.walkthrough: Raucle is a Scots word for rough, used by Walter Scott in his novel Rob Roy; this is its comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Raucle means rough or harsh in Scots, so raucler is the Scots comparative meaning rougher, as in Scott's Rob Roy.

clue.text: Veggies with leftovers

blocks.note: W is an abbreviation for with
orts are scraps of food left over from a meal

explanation.surface: A meal of vegetables served with the scraps from yesterday.
explanation.definitionFit: Wort is an old word for a plant or herb, especially a cabbage or other vegetable.

clue.text: Rev with needless ferocity turned on American blue trumpery

indicators.note: a word turned round faces the other way, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: to gun an engine is to rev it hard
A is an abbreviation for American
blue is the colour of the UK Conservative Party, whose members are Tories

explanation.surface: A clergyman with pointless savagery turns against a gloomy American over some trivial nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rev' looks like the clergyman abbreviation; it is revving an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory means worthless or of no value, which is what trumpery means as an adjective.

clue.text: Steady fruit of desert runs?

blocks.note: the date palm's fruit grows in desert oases
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A question about whether a dessert of fruit sets the stomach running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' invites a reading as 'dessert'; the date is simply the desert palm's fruit. 'Steady' is a noun for a regular partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady is a regular boyfriend or girlfriend, someone one is going out with, and a dater is a person who dates.

clue.text: Most jeer blooming amateur that swims the southern seas

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for the fish itself

indicators.note: most of a word means nearly all of it, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to barrack is to jeer at a speaker or player
flowers that are blooming are out
A is a standard abbreviation for amateur

explanation.surface: Spectators heckle some hopeless novice swimmer struggling in the cold oceans of the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' looks like a mild British swear word attached to 'amateur', but it supplies OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The barracouta is a long predatory fish found in southern-hemisphere waters, especially around Australia, New Zealand and South Africa.

clue.text: Irish bottled liquor, pretty much good though lacking power

definitions.note: bottled here is slang for drunk

indicators.note: pretty much means nearly all, so the preceding word loses its last letter
something lacking a part is missing it, so the abbreviation that follows is taken out

blocks.note: stock is the liquor in which meat or bones have been boiled
pious means devout, morally good
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: An Irish drinker who has bottled up some spirit is fairly well behaved, if a little feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquor' suggests alcohol, but here it is the cooking liquid called stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocious is Irish slang for very drunk, and bottled is also slang for being intoxicated.

clue.text: ____ means second spring in which stewards act for all (10, two words)

definitions.text: in which stewards act for all
definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for the workplace arrangement

blocks.note: an agency is a means by which something is done
S is the abbreviation for second
to hop is to spring or jump

explanation.surface: A blank waits to be filled with a means of jumping, under arrangements where officials speak for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank opening the clue stands for the answer itself, which the trailing clause describes.
explanation.definitionFit: In an agency shop a union bargains for all workers and non-members pay a fee, so union stewards represent everyone.

clue.text: From the east a cook finally supplies ____?

definitions.note: the blank asks what dish the cook supplies

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word it follows
in an across clue reading from the east means right to left, so everything runs backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of cook
kit is a set of supplies or equipment

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what some cook from the Orient ends up serving.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank works as the definition: the solver fills in what the cook supplies, a dish named by the very letters the wordplay builds, read from the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Tikka is a South Asian dish of meat marinated in spices and roasted, the sort of thing an eastern cook serves.

clue.text: Prudent hack admitted fighting tax

indicators.note: a word that has admitted something has let it inside

blocks.note: sage means wise or prudent
to hack is to cut roughly

explanation.surface: A careful journalist concedes that a war levy has been introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' reads as a journalist, but it is the verb meaning to chop.
explanation.definitionFit: Scutage was a feudal payment made by a vassal instead of personal military service, so it was a tax connected with fighting.

clue.text: Are wheels spinning under upset chuckle-head? A menace (8, two words)

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom up
spinning round turns something to face the opposite way, so these letters run backwards
in a down entry, what comes under another piece is placed after it

blocks.note: a yob is a loutish idiot, a chuckle-head
the blogger's tentative reading: this word is taken as RE
wheels is slang for a car

explanation.surface: A worried question whether some dimwit's car is skidding out of control, putting others in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is uncertain: the source's blogger suggested RE for 'Are' plus CAR, all reversed, below YOB reversed, and asked for better ideas. A boy racer is British slang for a young man who drives fast and showily.
explanation.definitionFit: Boy racers are young drivers who speed recklessly in souped-up cars, a menace on the roads.

clue.text: Badger without the benefit of quiet compound

indicators.note: going without the benefit of something means doing without it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: to badger someone is to pester them
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: An animal reduced to living without any peace in its den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning to nag.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is a chemical compound formed when an acid reacts with an alcohol.

clue.text: Utter failure to follow suit whipping off top

indicators.note: whipping off the top of a word removes its first letter

blocks.note: in card games a renounce is a failure to follow suit

explanation.surface: A complete failure to copy what others are wearing, with someone pulling off their shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective meaning complete, attached to 'failure', but it is the verb meaning to say. The card-game sense of renounce is playing a different suit from the one led.
explanation.definitionFit: To enounce is to pronounce or state something, which is to utter it.

clue.text: Combed disturbing notice on dead

indicators.note: something disturbing is moved out of place, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
D is an abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: An unsettling death notice has been searched through carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combed' looks like a verb meaning searched; it is an adjective meaning comb-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Ctenoid describes fish scales with a comb-like toothed edge, so it means having teeth like a comb.

clue.text: Graphic pictures I knock out not specified

blocks.note: taken as written
KO is the boxing abbreviation for a knockout
NS is an abbreviation for not specified

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of knocking out lurid images without saying which ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikons, a variant spelling of icons, are religious images, pictures painted on wood in the Orthodox tradition.

clue.text: Egyptian soul mate is a spiritual dancer

blocks.note: in ancient Egyptian belief the ka is the spiritual double or soul
china means mate, from rhyming slang china plate

explanation.surface: An ancient Egyptian's soulmate turns out to be a mystical dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang for mate: china plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A kachina is a Hopi ancestral spirit, and also a masked dancer who impersonates such a spirit in ceremonies.

clue.text: Well-rounded mock line used in gibe

indicators.note: pieces used in another word are set inside it

blocks.note: to ape is to mimic or mock
L is an abbreviation for line
a shy is a throw, and figuratively a jeer or gibe

explanation.surface: A derisive line delivered as part of a taunt is admired as a complete performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Shapely means having an attractive, curvy figure, which is well-rounded.

clue.text: Pull up Asian tethering emptied yacht (5, two words)

indicators.note: something tethering an object holds it fast within its grip, so it surrounds what follows
an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving only its outer letters

blocks.note: a Lao is a native of Laos
the outer letters of yacht

explanation.surface: An Asian sailor ties up a yacht with nothing aboard and brings it to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: In nautical language, to lay to is to bring a ship to a stop facing the wind, which is to pull up.

clue.text: Any of three leading Greeks is right to back restitution of chair

indicators.note: to back something is to move it backwards, so these letters are read right to left
a restitution puts things back together in a new state, so the letters of the next word are rebuilt

blocks.note: RT is an abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: One of three Greek leaders is entitled to support getting his seat of office back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greeks' reflects the word's Greek origin: a triumvirate of rulers in a Greek-derived term.
explanation.definitionFit: A triarch is one of three joint rulers of a triarchy, so any one of a governing trio.

clue.text: A coalition of Britain and America forms source of poison

blocks.note: taken as written
BR is an abbreviation for Britain or British
the US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A transatlantic political alliance turns out to be the root of something toxic.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrus is the plant genus that includes the rosary pea, whose bright seeds contain the deadly toxin abrin.

clue.text: Little over half of diversion is parrotry

indicators.note: keeping only a little over half of a word drops its front portion

blocks.note: escapism is a diversion from reality

explanation.surface: Mindless copying of others is just a bit more than half of an amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: Five of eight letters are kept, the back end.
explanation.definitionFit: Apism is aping, mere imitation, which is parrotry: copying without understanding.

clue.text: Universal chimney pot would've been behovely

blocks.note: U is the film certificate for universal
chimney pot is old slang for a top hat, and tile is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A standard chimney pot would have been just what was needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chimney pot' sounds like rooftop hardware, and a tile is roofing too, but both are slang for a hat. 'Would've been' marks the definition as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Utile is an obsolete word for useful, and behovely, itself archaic, means useful or needful.

clue.text: I collar horse dealers west of Newbury — with bow

indicators.note: the westernmost part of a word written across is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of Newbury
arco is the musical direction to play with the bow

explanation.surface: A speaker who arrests racehorse traders near the Berkshire racing town of Newbury, carrying a bow.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is slang for heroin, so the horse dealers are drug pushers, not racing folk around Newbury, a Berkshire racecourse town.
explanation.definitionFit: A narco is a US narcotics agent, whose job is arresting drug dealers, including those selling heroin.

clue.text: Prepayment lifted on small vessels which are lit up

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means raised up the column, so the word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: an ante is a stake paid before the deal in poker
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: An advance payment is raised on some small boats that are illuminated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests ships, but these are small heating containers.
explanation.definitionFit: An etna is a small vessel for heating liquids over a spirit lamp, so it is a container that is lit.

clue.text: Prized metal previously left in shallow pan

indicators.note: one item put in another goes inside it

blocks.note: a patina is a shallow dish or pan of ancient Rome
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A valued bit of metal was formerly left lying in a cooking dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Previously' belongs to the definition, marking an old name.
explanation.definitionFit: Platina is the older name for platinum, a precious metal.

clue.text: French char looking at special ham?

blocks.note: char is British slang for tea, and the French for tea is thé
SP is an abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: A French cook eyes a particularly fine ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' reads as a cleaning lady or a fish, but it is British slang for tea. 'Ham' looks like meat on the menu; it is a bad actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesp is an informal word for an actor, and a ham is an actor who overplays, so the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: Roller signalled by my unrivalled place in the market

blocks.note: both my! and cor! are exclamations of surprise
a niche is a specialised corner of the market with no competitors

explanation.surface: A luxury car announced by its peerless market position.
explanation.walkthrough: A Roller is British slang for a Rolls-Royce car, and Corniche was the name of one of its models.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rolls-Royce Corniche was a luxury convertible, so it is a particular Roller.

clue.text: Clean slips being disturbed? Preferably not in this game

definitions.note: a cryptic description pointing to the game

indicators.note: something disturbed is knocked out of its order, so the words before it are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cleanly removing slivers without moving the others: the whole point of this game is avoiding disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface describes the game itself: players lift slips from a pile, and disturbing the rest is what to avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: Spellicans is another name for spillikins, a game of picking thin sticks off a heap without moving the others.

clue.text: Result in islanders dying off in scores

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: the Moros are Muslim peoples of the southern Philippine islands
an end is an outcome or result

explanation.surface: Something causes island people to die in their dozens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scores' looks like a number of twenties; it means pieces of written music.
explanation.definitionFit: Morendo is a musical direction meaning gradually dying away in tone and tempo, written in musical scores.

clue.text: Mushy peas reportedly in part of decision

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling
one item placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: having a say is having a part in a decision
the plural of the letter P is pronounced like peas

explanation.surface: A sloppy dish of mushy peas, described as forming part of the verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: Mushy peas is a British side dish of mashed marrowfat peas, which makes 'Mushy' look like part of the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappy means soppily sentimental, which is mushy in the emotional sense.
